$comment: The shrink-only ratchet for inert light-mode story wrappers (#93, #77).
`<div data-theme="light">` around a story activates NOTHING: @spec-kitty/tokens anchors its
light block on `:root[data-theme="light"], .sk-light`, and `:root` only ever matches <html>.
The story renders the DARK palette on a light background and every gate stays green — axe
included, because the contrast it measures is the dark palette's and that is fine.
TEN, AND THE NUMBER MAY ONLY FALL. #77 migrated grid and section-banner and fixed those two
on the way past; the ten below are the remainder, all in packages/styles. They are #78's and
#79's to retire as those missions convert their components — lower the count in the same
commit that fixes them, which is what makes the improvement a deliberate line in the diff
rather than a silent one.
WHY A COUNT AND NOT A DIRECTORY SCOPE. The first version of this gate scanned
packages/elements/** only, on the theory that each batch mission would widen it. A pass-2
lens showed that model had already failed twice before it was written: sk-stub and
sk-nav-pill are both MIGRATED elements whose styles-layer stories still offend. Migrating a
component does not move its styles-layer story into the elements directory, so a directory
scope keeps missing exactly the files it exists to catch — while
docs/contributing/adding-a-component.md tells authors to fix "the styles-layer story".
WHY A COUNT AND NOT AN ALLOWLIST. Same reason expected-parts.json and .wrapper-floor are
counts: a path list rots on every rename and invites an entry being added rather than a bug
being fixed. A count cannot be added to.

#78 retires feature-card's and ribbon-card's, 10 -> 8. blog-card's does NOT follow in this mission: that component is deferred pending an operator ruling (see #78), so its wrapper is one of the eight that remain.

#79 retires all three of its own components' wrappers — pill-tag, button and check-bullet — 8 -> 5. An earlier revision of this line claimed button and check-bullet 'follow in the same mission' while leaving both in place, and the button one sat in a line region that same PR had edited for the class rename; three pre-merge lenses caught the false claim. Retiring pill-tag's is also what EXPOSED a real WCAG failure the inert wrapper had been hiding: the tinted variants paired dark-tuned inks with pastel light tints at 1.51:1. Five remain: blog-card, form-field, nav-pill, site-footer and the styles-layer stub.
#78 retires blog-card's while rewriting its story onto the generated exports, 5 -> 4. Four remain: form-field (#141), nav-pill, site-footer (#77) and the styles-layer stub.

#77 retires site-footer's, taking the count 4 -> 3. The three that remain are form-field, nav-pill and stub — NOT blog-card, which #78 already retired and which an earlier revision of this note wrongly listed. A lens caught it; that is the fourth time in this programme a ratchet note has named different data than the ratchet holds, which is an argument for deriving these lists rather than typing them. Measured before assuming: site-footer's inks are --sk-fg-muted at 6.20:1 and --sk-fg-default at 16.03:1 on the light page, so unlike pill-tag (four variants at 1.51-2.48:1) and check-bullet (1.73:1) this wrapper was hiding nothing. The difference is not luck — site-footer styles with SEMANTIC --sk-fg-* tokens, while the two that failed paired raw --sk-color-* palette values against tint surfaces. That is the shape to look for in the three that are left.

RETIRED FOR form-field AT #141, 3 -> 2. The wrapper was a <div data-theme="light"> and therefore inert: tokens anchor the light block on :root[data-theme="light"], .sk-light, and :root only ever matches <html>. Removing the attribute changes nothing visually — which is the point, and why it was safe to do in the commit that closes this component out. The remaining two are nav-pill and stub. NOT DONE, and filed rather than left implicit: making this story GENUINELY light-mode (a .sk-light wrapper) is a separate change, and the log above records that doing exactly that for pill-tag exposed a real 1.51:1 contrast failure it had been hiding. sk-form-field.css has the same shape the log names — .sk-form-field--error .sk-form-field__description uses a raw var(--sk-color-red) against a tint surface — and it should be measured by someone who can run axe.
